Expected packets worked out from OpenRGB's C++ (commit d4798c120659ec5ba2e664a9e87bedff8d36f880, Controllers/SteelSeriesController) by a separate reference model that mirrors each C++ function buffer by buffer (openrgb-work/steelseries/gen_fixtures.py in the porting session's scratch space, not part of the repository); plugin.js was never run to make them. 'products' comes from SteelSeriesControllerDetect.cpp (first registration wins for a pid, as in OpenRGB). Each variant lists the LED names and grid cells (zones in OpenRGB order; a zone with several LEDs gets its own row, consecutive one-LED zones share a row), two colour sets in LED order, and the I/O for Initialize (switch to Direct), a frame with each colour set and Shutdown. ops: write = output report (hid_write), send_report = feature report (hid_send_feature_report), read = input report read (hid_read_timeout), pause = sleep; hex is the whole buffer at the length the C++ passes, report id first. A product with 'held_back' is one OpenRGB lists that the Lightloom plugin deliberately does not claim (the reason is given). Deliberate Lightloom deviations from the C++ that the hardware notes describe are modelled the same way here (Apex M750 numeric-pad slots, Aerox receiver read timeout).
